input_weight_pool1.meaning: user-supplied input weight for pool1 in the weight array

input_weight_pool2.meaning: user-supplied input weight for pool2 in the weight array

input_weight_pool3.meaning: user-supplied input weight for pool3 in the weight array

pool2_gauge_killed_before_vote.meaning: pool2's gauge is killed before the owner invokes vote

total_weight_base_small.meaning: the user provides a very small total weight base (qualitative; no numeric bound stated)

allocation_matches_input_weights.meaning: the allocated voting power per pool corresponds to the user's input weights (no deviation from intended distribution)

assumptions: The owner is the voter who invokes vote with the weight array.
The example weight array [10, 30, 60] is illustrative of the input weights for pool1, pool2, pool3.
The killed pool2 gauge is skipped during allocation, so weights are recalculated over remaining pools.
The exact recalculation mechanism is described only by example and not fully specified.

unresolved.description: No numeric bound is given for what constitutes a 'very small total weight base' or the validation threshold.
The report does not give a numeric definition of the intended per-pool allocation or the magnitude of deviation, so the correspondence is represented qualitatively.

limitations: The allocation correspondence is encoded as a qualitative Boolean because the report provides no numeric allocation formula or deviation magnitude.
Only the pool1 input weight literal (10) is bound; pool2 and pool3 weights are declared but not constrained by a selected precondition predicate.
The report does not state who may call vote; only the owner scenario is formalized.
